message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points are tallied from the cards left in opponents’ hands when someone goes “Uno.” | | **Setup** | • 108‑card deck (standard Uno).
• Each player draws 7 cards.
• Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card to start the discard pile; if it’s a special card, follow its effect immediately. | | **Turn Order** | Clockwise (unless a Reverse card changes direction). | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play one card that matches either the **color** or the **number/symbol** of the top discard. If you can’t play, you must draw one card. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and skips their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color and the next player draws four cards. (Can only be played if you have no matching color; otherwise you risk a challenge.) | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you have **exactly one card left**, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards their last card. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards still held by the other players: numbers = face value, Draw Two/Reverse/Skip = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Winning the Game** | First to reach the target score (usually 500) wins. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep track of the current color** – it’s the key to deciding what you can play. 2. **Use Wild cards strategically** – change the color to something you’re holding or to trap opponents. 3. **Watch for “Draw Four” challenges** – if you suspect a player lied, you can challenge them; they must show their hand. If they were lying, you draw four instead of them. 4. **Plan ahead** – try to get rid of high‑value cards early so you don’t lose many points if you’re forced to draw. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
